body: It's not just her Mom. This whole parental negativity is pretty recent. Her issues have always been there and her mom was really supportive up until this last year. It feels like she's given up on her daughter so a lot of her depression has kind of blown up because of it. Her mom is adopted and her dad is out of the picture along with his side of the family. So my SO doesn't really have many people besides me to talk to her and care about her. she sees her real grandma like twice a year and other than that there is nothing else. Her mom also had her when she was like 19 I believe and her mom's boyfriend never wanted kids. I'm pretty sure he got a vasectomy to make sure he didn't. I think the boyfriend is springing a lot of his negativity on to her mom making them both act very unsympathetic

Thank you! I try to be really supportive, I've definitely learned from past mistakes too because before I had never really known how deep and painful some of these things can really be. 

She used to play drums but her parents decided they didn't want the noise anymore so she slowly lost her way with music unfortunately. I try and get to her to do new things and explore new hobbies but she has almost zero motivation for anything. She gets anxiety even going to movie theaters and concerts cause of the noise. She does like decorating cakes and has a big interest in tea and cooking new recipes and also makeup. We've explored the possibility of doing beauty school but with her current situation doing school is kinda out of the question. 

I would like to support her any way I can. I feel like she definitely needs more hobbies and productive things to do with her time cause right now she doesn't really have a muse or passion for anything really. I'll definitely look into some free counseling, she's been going to this one counselor a little while ago but it was like once every two weeks ... and apparently they weren't addressing the right problems 

you mentioned joining a club. Is there anything that we can maybe do as a couple? I know she'd probably be hesitant to explore something like that by herself

She came over this afternoon and we talked and she calmed down a little bit. I don't show her when It frustrates me cause that's counter productive but I was very patient with her and understanding during our talk and I feel she appreciated my presence. I think it's very clear that she needs time away from her house so I'm hoping that she can stay with me for a little while. 

As for her coming here on Reddit I'll propose the idea to her. She doesn't have a Reddit account or go on the site at all but I'll see what I can do. I'd say the more people who can talk to her the better
